shop.title: Make it read like a shop, not an audit
shop.blurb: Turn a careful source register into a page a buyer can act on.

findable.title: Make it findable
findable.blurb: Give search engines one site to index and a reason to rank it.

machinery.title: Make the machinery trustworthy
machinery.blurb: Automate the parts that can be automated, and put a gate in front of the parts that cannot.

publication.title: Make it read like a publication
publication.blurb: Authorship, navigation, brand, imagery, seasons and clusters: the changes that make the site feel published rather than generated.

Q-T50-02.what_we_know: The owner supplied the tracking ID shopnow047c-20 in the brief. Since PR #160 (T61) it is on every product button this site writes, applied by the policy-guarded link builder. The five supplied short links do not carry it: they are Amazon's own redirects, and no resolved URL carried a tag when re-observed on 2026-11-19.

suggestions.title: Show real product images, from a source the account is allowed to use
suggestions.summary: Every card on the front page is text-only. Shoppers expect to see the thing. Amazon's program policies govern how its content, images included, may be used off Amazon, and which mechanism this account can use is not known yet.

options.label: A
options.text: Stay text-only, with simple category icons.
options.tradeoff: Clean and safe, but reads less like a shop.

options.label: B
options.text: Use images served through an Amazon mechanism the account is entitled to, once Q-T66-01 confirms which one.
options.cost: One build pass once access is confirmed
options.tradeoff: Depends on account entitlements nobody has checked yet.

options.label: C
options.text: Buy the products and take our own photographs.
options.cost: The products plus a photo session
options.tradeoff: Best for trust and originality; slowest, and needs Q-T66-05.

suggestions.title: Add hands-on notes from someone who has used the products
suggestions.summary: Today every write-up compares what the maker and the listing promise. Google's guidance asks whether content offers original information and whether it is clear who made it and how. First-hand use is the one ingredient this site cannot produce from spec sheets.

options.label: A
options.text: Stay spec-led and say so plainly on every write-up.
options.tradeoff: Honest but interchangeable with every other spec roundup.

options.label: B
options.text: Buy the five, use them for two weeks, and add a short dated 'what we noticed' block with our own photos to each write-up.
options.tradeoff: Strongest signal for readers and search; needs a named author and a budget.

options.label: C
options.text: Summarise other sites' reviews.
options.tradeoff: Thin, derivative, and exactly what the guidance warns against.

suggestions.title: Decide what the ThermoMaven button should open now that Amazon shows a newer model
suggestions.summary: On 2026-11-19 the listing the supplied link opens (B0DHZTCNR5) carried a 'There is a newer model of this item' notice pointing to B0GL7Z4KP4 (Orange). Whether that is a new revision or a colour variant was not verified.

options.label: A
options.text: Keep linking the listing the supplied short link opens.
options.tradeoff: Matches what the owner supplied; might point buyers at an older model.

options.label: B
options.text: Switch to B0GL7Z4KP4 after reading and sourcing its listing.
options.tradeoff: Overrides the supplied link without the owner saying so.

options.label: C
options.text: Show both, labelled.
options.tradeoff: More choice, more clutter.

suggestions.title: Verify the site in Google Search Console and submit the sitemap
suggestions.summary: Without a verified Search Console property there is no query data at all, so SG-T50-04's 'choose the next topic from measured queries' cannot start. Verification can be done with an HTML file or an HTML tag, both of which this repository can publish.

options.label: A
options.text: Do nothing and rely on crawling.
options.tradeoff: No idea what anyone searches for.

options.label: B
options.text: Owner creates the property; we commit the verification file or tag and submit sitemap.xml.
options.tradeoff: Needs the owner's Google account.

suggestions.title: Move to a real domain name
suggestions.summary: The site lives at a GitHub sub-path. GitHub Pages supports custom domains, and GitHub recommends a www subdomain and verifying the domain first.

options.label: A
options.text: Stay on kanlerxz87-cyber.github.io/Zone2.
options.tradeoff: Looks like a project, not a publication.

options.label: B
options.text: Register a domain, verify it with GitHub, and serve the site on its www subdomain.
options.cost: Domain registration plus one DNS change
options.tradeoff: Every canonical URL changes once; worth doing before traffic arrives, not after.

suggestions.title: Take the old builds and duplicate dashboards out of the search index
suggestions.summary: The repository publishes close to two hundred pages across a dozen namespaces, most of them earlier builds and internal review surfaces. A reader-facing site competes with its own scaffolding. Google honours a noindex meta tag page by page, which works on GitHub Pages.

options.label: A
options.text: Keep everything indexable.
options.tradeoff: Search engines see far more audit pages than buyer pages.

options.label: B
options.text: Add noindex to legacy and internal namespaces; keep them reachable from the footer index.
options.tradeoff: Nothing is lost; those pages simply stop competing in search.

options.label: C
options.text: Delete them from the published site; git history keeps them.
options.tradeoff: Cleanest, but breaks any bookmarks.

suggestions.title: Publish ahead of the season instead of on the day
suggestions.summary: Gift guides and holiday cooking questions are searched before the day, not on it. T66 published the turkey guide on 2026-11-19, a week before Thanksgiving (2026-11-26), as a first example. Next up are the December holidays and New Year.

options.label: A
options.text: Evergreen guides only.
options.tradeoff: Misses the weeks when people are actually shopping.

options.label: B
options.text: A light seasonal calendar: one piece two to three weeks before each major cooking or gifting date, each tied to a product we cover.
options.tradeoff: Needs someone to keep the calendar.

options.label: C
options.text: Chase daily trends.
options.tradeoff: Unsustainable and off-topic for five products.

suggestions.title: Re-check the five supplied links on a schedule and open an issue when one changes
suggestions.summary: Every destination on this site rests on five short links resolving to the same listings. They have done so on every date checked, most recently 2026-11-19, but nothing watches them between sessions. GitHub Actions workflows can run at a scheduled time.

options.label: A
options.text: Keep checking by hand when a session happens to run.
options.tradeoff: A changed destination could sit unnoticed for days.

options.label: B
options.text: A weekly scheduled workflow that resolves the five links and opens an issue if any destination ASIN changes.
options.tradeoff: Amazon may rate-limit automated requests, so a failed check has to be read as 'unknown', not 'changed'.

suggestions.title: Keep one register of product facts, not two
suggestions.summary: marketing/data/facts.json (used by the reader pages) and ledger/products.json (used by the dashboards) were transcribed separately and now disagree. For the 8-quart Chefman's power, facts.json says 'verified, 1700 W / 120 V' while the ledger records a CONFLICT, because an Amazon bullet says 1000 W (flag F-46).

options.label: A
options.text: Keep both and reconcile by hand.
options.tradeoff: They will drift again.

options.label: B
options.text: Make ledger/products.json the single source and generate facts.json from it.
options.tradeoff: Touches two namespaces at once.

options.label: C
options.text: Make facts.json the source instead.
options.tradeoff: facts.json has fewer fields, so the ledger would lose detail.

suggestions.title: Put a name on the writing and add an About page
suggestions.summary: Every page is signed 'Counter Notes'. Google's guidance asks readers' questions of every page: who made it, how, and why. An About page that says who picks the products, how they are checked, and that the links earn a commission answers all three.

options.label: A
options.text: Stay unsigned.
options.tradeoff: Reads as anonymous and generated.

options.label: B
options.text: A named editor with a short bio on every guide, plus an About page.
options.cost: One page plus a byline field
options.tradeoff: Needs a real person willing to be named.

options.label: C
options.text: A pen name with an honest About page.
options.tradeoff: Better than nothing, weaker than a real name.

suggestions.title: Give returning readers a way to follow along
suggestions.summary: An RSS feed exists (marketing/feed.xml), but it lists only the marketing topic pages; the root guides are not in it. An email list would reach more people but needs a provider, a privacy notice and somewhere to store addresses, which static hosting cannot provide by itself.

options.label: A
options.text: Extend RSS to cover every guide (one feed for the whole site) and link it from every footer.
options.cost: One generator change in build_marketing.py, which another session owns
options.tradeoff: Few readers use RSS, but it costs almost nothing.

options.label: B
options.text: An email newsletter through a third-party provider, with a privacy notice.
options.cost: Provider account and a privacy page
options.tradeoff: Adds a data processor; pointless before there is traffic.

suggestions.title: Treat thermometers as a second category, paired with air fryers
suggestions.summary: Two of the five supplied links open meat thermometers, not air fryers. T66 gave them a category page and three guides, one of which joins the two categories (using a thermometer in an air fryer). Whether thermometers were intended at all is still Q-T50-01.

options.label: A
options.text: Keep both categories and build the 'air fryer plus probe' cluster.
options.tradeoff: Broader site, still coherent: both are countertop cooking.

options.label: B
options.text: Split thermometers into their own site.
options.tradeoff: Splits the little authority the domain has.

options.label: C
options.text: Drop the thermometers.
options.tradeoff: Ignores two of the five supplied links.

suggestions.title: Pick one home for the thermometer guides
suggestions.summary: Two sessions published thermometer pages on 2026-11-19 without seeing each other's work: T64 under marketing/thermometers/ (a category page, two product pages, four guides) and T66 under guides/thermometers*.html (a category page and three guides). Three topics overlap (turkey placement, instant-read or leave-in, thermometers in an air fryer). The figures agree; each pair cites the same FoodSafety.gov and USDA FSIS pages. Until this is decided, every T66 guide links its T64 counterpart and the T66 category page links T64's desk. Flag F-50. Recommendation B: T64's section is the broader one (product pages and an accuracy guide as well) and is already in the RSS feed; T66's food-safety chart and front-page shelf can move with it.

options.label: A
options.text: Keep both sets, cross-linked as they are now.
options.cost: None now; every edit is made twice
options.tradeoff: Two pages per question compete with each other in search and can drift apart.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep T64's marketing/thermometers/ as the home; turn the three T66 guides into short pointers (or remove them) and send the reader menu's 'Meat thermometers' link there.
options.cost: One session; the sitemap and both gates change
options.tradeoff: Loses T66's food-safety chart and front-page shelf unless they are moved across.

options.label: C
options.text: Keep T66's guides/ as the home; merge T64's unique pages (product pages, the accuracy check) into it.
options.cost: One session; build_thermometers.py and verify_marketing change
options.tradeoff: Touches another session's generator and its gates.

questions.question: Can this Associates account show Amazon product images, and through which tool?
questions.what_we_know: The site shows no product images. Amazon's program policies govern how Amazon content, images included, may be used off Amazon.
questions.what_is_missing: Which tools this account is actually entitled to use, and whether the account is approved (Q-T50-04).
questions.how_to_discover: Sign in to Associates Central, check which link and image tools and API access the account has, and record the answer here.

questions.question: Is there a domain name for this site, and who will own it?
questions.what_we_know: The site is served from a github.io sub-path. GitHub Pages supports apex and www custom domains and recommends verifying the domain first.
questions.what_is_missing: Whether the owner has or wants a domain, which name, and who pays for it.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision. If yes: register it, verify it in GitHub settings, then we add the CNAME and update every canonical URL in one pass.

questions.question: Which Google account will own the site in Search Console?
questions.what_we_know: A sitemap derived from the tree and a robots.txt are published. Search Console supports HTML-file and HTML-tag verification, both of which this repository can publish.
questions.what_is_missing: A verified property. Without one there is no data on which searches show this site or get clicked.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner adds the property in Search Console and sends the verification token; we commit it and submit sitemap.xml.

questions.question: Who is the named author, and have they used any of the five products?
questions.what_we_know: Every page is currently signed with the site name only. Google's helpful-content guidance asks who created a page and how.
questions.what_is_missing: A name, a two-line bio, and an honest statement of hands-on experience (or none).
questions.how_to_discover: Owner supplies them; we add a byline and an About page.

questions.question: Is there a budget to buy the products for hands-on testing?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing on this site comes from first-hand use; every claim is the maker's or the listing's.
questions.what_is_missing: A budget, and someone with the kitchen and the time.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner decision. Start with the one product where a hands-on note would settle the most: the 8-quart Chefman, where two official pages disagree on wattage.

questions.question: Does anyone still rely on the old builds and internal dashboards being indexed by search engines?
questions.what_we_know: About a dozen namespaces (northstar/, zone2/, research-hub/, affiliate-lab/, revalidation/, review pages and others) are published alongside the reader pages. Google drops a page carrying a noindex tag from its results, page by page.
questions.what_is_missing: Whether any of them is linked from outside or used by anyone, which Search Console would show (Q-T66-03).
questions.how_to_discover: Owner confirms; after Search Console is verified, its page-indexing report shows which of them are indexed or receive clicks.

questions.question: Should the ThermoMaven button follow Amazon's 'newer model' notice?
questions.what_we_know: On 2026-11-19 the supplied link opened B0DHZTCNR5, and that listing showed 'There is a newer model of this item' pointing to B0GL7Z4KP4 (Orange).
questions.what_is_missing: The owner's intent, and whether B0GL7Z4KP4 is a revision or a colour variant. Its listing has not been read or sourced.
questions.how_to_discover: Owner confirms which listing they mean; if it is the newer one, we read and source that listing before switching.

food_safety_note: Rows transcribed from the FoodSafety.gov chart (FS1), page states it was last reviewed November 21, 2024, read 2026-11-19.
